If one says, 'Why was it not spoken thus: "should be passed into nirvāṇa"?' It is in order to clear away the first dhyāna and so forth. Because they are without the afflictions of the lower levels, the Bhagavan spoke of them as enumerations of nirvāṇa. If one says, 'Why was "into the expanse of nirvāṇa with remainder of aggregates" not spoken?' It is because the remainder of the aggregates of suffering has not been abandoned. The intention of bodhisattvas to bring all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa should be seen by means of three causes: waiting for another time for those born in unfree states, and the state of being unfree being merely what one prays for in order to indicate it, but it is not limited to that, because complete nirvāṇa is impossible for those abiding there; completely ripening those who are not completely ripened; and liberating those who are completely ripened; therefore, they are not unable to be sought. By this intention to bring sentient beings without exception to complete nirvāṇa, the extensiveness of the mind of awakening is taught. Here, how one should abide by means of both aspiration and prayer is also taught. Now, in order to teach how one should accomplish it by how one enters meditative equipoise in yoga, 'thus' and so forth were spoken. 'Thus, even though conventionally all sentient beings are passed into complete nirvāṇa, how does the bodhisattva ultimately not observe any sentient being? It is because they do not exist'—thus one should individually investigate it by entering meditative equipoise in yoga.

That which is the generation of the mind upon arising, thinking, 'Ultimately, not any sentient being has been passed into complete nirvāṇa by me'—by this the profound is taught, and the ultimate mind of awakening is also taught. By the former, the conventional is taught. Now, in order to teach how the mind should be completely held here by cutting off distraction, 'Why is that?' was stated. 'If' is to be connected with the meaning of 'what if'.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: There is no postulating that Devadatta is bound and later Yajñadatta is liberated. Nor is there the experiencing by one of the fruit of karma done by another. Because it would become an extreme absurdity, and it would logically follow that what is done is wasted and one meets with what is not done; thus, because that which is the moment of consciousness imputed as the agent has no connection with the fruit, there is the fault of what is done being wasted; and because precisely that which is not the agent is connected with the fruit, there also becomes the fault of meeting with what is not done. Remembering and so forth are also not renowned in the world as having different bases. If one asks, 'Well then, how is it?', they have precisely a single basis: what is experienced by the mind of Devadatta is not remembered or recognized by the mind of Yajñadatta, but it is renowned that whatever experiences it, that itself remembers and recognizes. Therefore, there exists a single person who follows along all occasions. The syllogism is: 'Whatever are bound and liberated, those have a single basis, like for example Devadatta being bound by iron fetters and being liberated; and both being bound and being liberated, which have become the basis of debate, are also being bound and being liberated'—this is a reason of nature. Similarly, for establishing the agent as having precisely a single basis, one should also investigate the syllogism,' they say.

If one says, 'Even though an excellent fruit exists, because one is unable to attain it, one seeks it in that way': according to your system, because there are three lineages and also those without lineage, even an inferior fruit cannot be attained by everyone. However, the two lineages of bodhisattvas are like this: by the power of which, those who are overwhelmed by the force of great compassion abandon such considerations as thinking, 'Is this possible?' and thinking, 'While other Buddhas and bodhisattvas who act for the benefit of others also reside here, what is the use of my making a meaningless prayer?'; and, having cast away reliance on others, those who are held by great compassion, seeing beings afflicted by the blazing fire of suffering, make the prayer thinking thus: 'I alone will protect them'; if one says it is as was explained: 'Having completely abandoned the conceptualization thinking "Is it difficult or not difficult?", you yourself promised: "These beings are distressed,"' even if that is so, why would one not make a prayer precisely for the excellent one that cannot be attained, like praying for a beloved son to become king? Why would one seek only the inferior? Therefore, it is logical that non-abiding nirvāṇa itself is the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates here, because in it there is no remainder of contaminated aggregates.

If one says, 'Why was it not spoken thus: "should be passed into nirvāṇa"?' It is in order to clear away the first dhyāna and so forth. Because they are without the afflictions of the lower levels, the Bhagavan spoke of them as enumerations of nirvāṇa. If one says, 'Why was "into the expanse of nirvāṇa with remainder of aggregates" not spoken?' It is because the remainder of the aggregates of suffering has not been abandoned. The intention of bodhisattvas to bring all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa should be seen by means of three causes: waiting for another time for those born in unfree states, and the state of being unfree being merely what one prays for in order to indicate it, but it is not limited to that, because complete nirvāṇa is impossible for those abiding there; completely ripening those who are not completely ripened; and liberating those who are completely ripened; therefore, they are not unable to be sought. By this intention to bring sentient beings without exception to complete nirvāṇa, the extensiveness of the mind of awakening is taught. Here, how one should abide by means of both aspiration and prayer is also taught. Now, in order to teach how one should accomplish it by how one enters meditative equipoise in yoga, 'thus' and so forth were spoken. 'Thus, even though conventionally all sentient beings are passed into complete nirvāṇa, how does the bodhisattva ultimately not observe any sentient being? It is because they do not exist'—thus one should individually investigate it by entering meditative equipoise in yoga.

'If' is to be connected with the meaning of 'what if'.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: Regarding that, if here one establishes a person and a sovereign one that is ultimate, permanent, and single, then at that time, because a connection together between such a person and the reason is not established anywhere, it is inconclusive. Because all formations are momentary, Devadatta and so forth are not established in the nature of being permanent and single, so the example also lacks what is to be established. For that very reason, the reason is contradictory, because it is connected with the opposite of that. However, if for some reason one establishes merely that they have a single basis, at that time it is establishing what is already established, for by that, too, it is indeed asserted that being bound and so forth have a single basis due to existing in a single continuum. Thus, at whatever time, in whatever continuum, those which have become cause and fruit, ignorance and so forth, arise continuously without the continuum being interrupted, at that time one designates it as 'being bound'. Moreover, when the noble path arises in that very [continuum] by degrees through hearing and so forth, and through the cessation of ignorance and so forth a transformation of basis occurs, it is designated as 'being liberated', but there is no establishing that those two possess an object that is an ultimate, permanent, single entity, because worldly being bound and being liberated are also similar to that. In whatever continuum a virtuous or non-virtuous mind and experience have arisen, in that very [continuum] at another time, in dependence upon the continuum having completely ripened—like the complete ripening of the continuum of a mātuluṅga and so forth that has been smeared with the juice of lac and so forth—because fruits such as happiness, suffering, and remembering appear to arise, virtue and so forth are renowned as having a single basis; but there is not any single agent, enjoyer, or rememberer, because all these imputed conventions are thoroughly distinguished merely by cause and fruit.

འོ་ན་སུ་གང་ཟག་ལ་སོགས་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་འཇུག་པ་དེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའམ་ཅི་ན། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་སེམས་ཅན་སྨོས་པ་དེ་ཁོ་ན་མཛད་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས་ཤིང་། ཡང་ཅིའི་སླད་དུ་ཞེས་ཞུས་པ་དང་། ཅིག་ཤོས་ཀྱིས་ཀྱང་མི་བྱའོ་ཞེས་གསུངས་སོ། །དགོངས་པ་ནི་འདི་ཡིན་ཏེ། བློ་གྲོས་ངན་པ་དག་གི་ཡང་དེ་ནི་ཕུང་པོར་ལས་གཞན་པ་ནང་ན་བྱ་བ་དང་། ལོངས་སྤྱོད་བཞི་པོ་བྱེད་པའི་སྐྱེས་བུ་ཞིག་ཡོད་པར་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་ནས་སེམས་ཅན་དང་སྲོག་ལ་སོགས་པའི་སྒྲར་ཐ་སྙད་འདོགས་པ་དང་། གང་དག་ཡང་གང་ཟག་བརྗོད་དུ་མི་རུང་བར་འདོད་པ་དེ་དག་གི་ཡང་དེ་ནི་ཕུང་པོར་གཏོགས་པའི་ཆོས་དང་མཚན་ཉིད་མི་འདྲ་བར་ཁས་བླངས་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཤུགས་ཀྱིས་དོན་གཞན་པ་ཁོ་ནར་ཁས་བླངས་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱང་བརྗོད་དུ་མི་རུང་བར་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་དངོས་པོ་ནི་ནམ་ཡང་བརྗོད་དུ་མི་རུང་བ་མི་སྲིད་དོ། །དེ་ནི་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚད་མ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་དང་། གནོད་པ་ཅན་ཡང་ཡོད་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེར་ལྟ་བའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ནི་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ལ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པས་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཁོ་ནར་འགྱུར་རོ། །གང་ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་དེ་དོན་དམ་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། གཞན་ན་རེ་བདག་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚད་མ་ཡོད་པ་ཁོ་ན་ཡིན་ནམ། འདི་ལྟར་བཅིངས་པ་དང་། ཐར་པ་དང་། ལམ་དང་། འབྲས་བུ་འབྲེལ་པ་དང་། དྲན་པ་དང་། ངོ་ཤེས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ནི་གཞི་གཅིག་པ་གྲགས་པ་དག་ཡིན་ན། བདག་མེད་པར་སྨྲ་བ་ཁྱེད་ཀྱི་ལུགས་ལྟར་ན་དེ་དག་གི་གཞིར་འགྲུབ་པར་འགྱུར་བ་གང་ཡིན་པ་གཅིག་པུ་ནི་འགའ་ཡང་མེད་ན་གཞིར་འགྱུར་བ་གང་ཞིག་ཡིན། རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པའི་སྐད་ཅིག་མ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྐད་ཅིག་སོ་སོ་ནི་ཐ་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །

If one says, 'Well then, is whoever engages in the notion of a person and so forth called a bodhisattva or what?', thinking, 'Why did he make mention of only "sentient being"?', one asked, 'Moreover, why?', and the other also stated, 'they are not to be.' The intention is this: those of bad intellect, having completely imagined that inside, other than the aggregates, there exists a person who performs actions and the four enjoyments, designate conventions with terms like 'sentient being' and 'living being' and so forth; and for those who assert an inexpressible person, too, because they have accepted it as having dissimilar characteristics from the dharmas included in the aggregates, by implication they have accepted it as precisely a different entity; because it would logically follow that everything is inexpressible, an inexpressible thing is never possible. Because there is no valid cognition that establishes it, and because there are also things that invalidate it, a bodhisattva who views it thus, due to manifestly adhering to a distortion, becomes precisely distorted. How could one who has become distorted become an ultimate bodhisattva? Others say, 'Is it not that there is indeed a valid cognition that establishes the self? Since being bound, being liberated, the path, connection with the fruit, remembering, recognizing, and so forth are renowned as having a single basis, according to your system which asserts no-self, if there is not any single thing that would be established as their basis, what would be the basis? Because the individual moments of the moments of consciousness are different.'

ལྷ་སྦྱིན་བཅིངས་ལ་ཕྱིས་མཆོད་སྦྱིན་གྲོལ་བར་རྣམ་པར་གཞག་པ་ནི་མེད་དོ། །གཞན་གྱིས་བྱས་པའི་ལས་ཀྱི་འབྲས་བུ་གཞན་གྱིས་མྱོང་བ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་དང་། བྱས་པ་ཆུད་ཟ་ཞིང་མ་བྱས་པ་དང་ཕྲད་པར་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་ཏེ། འདི་ལྟར་བྱེད་པ་པོར་བཏགས་པའི་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པའི་སྐད་ཅིག་མ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་དང་།འབྲས་བུ་འབྲེལ་བ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་བྱས་པ་ཆུད་ཟ་བའི་སྐྱོན་དང་། བྱེད་པ་པོ་མ་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ཁོ་ན་དང་འབྲས་བུ་འབྲེལ་པའི་ཕྱིར་མ་བྱས་པ་དང་། ཕྲད་པའི་སྐྱོན་དུ་ཡང་འགྱུར་རོ། །དྲན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཡང་འཇིག་རྟེན་ན་གནས་ཐ་དད་པར་མ་གྲགས་ཏེ། འོ་ན་ཇི་ལྟ་ཞེ་ན། གནས་གཅིག་པ་ཁོ་ན་སྟེ། ལྷ་སྦྱིན་གྱི་སེམས་ཀྱིས་མྱོང་བ་ནི་མཆོད་སྦྱིན་གྱི་སེམས་ཀྱིས་དྲན་པའམ་ངོ་ཤེས་པ་མེད་ཀྱི། གང་གིས་མྱོང་བ་དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་དྲན་ཞིང་ངོ་ཤེས་སོ་ཞེས་གྲགས་སོ། །དེ་བས་ན་སྐྱེས་བུ་གཅིག་པུ་གནས་སྐབས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ་ཞིག་ཡོད་དོ། །སྦྱོར་བ་ནི་བཅིངས་པ་དང་ཐར་པ་གང་དག་ཡིན་པ་དེ་དག་ནི་གཞི་གཅིག་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་ལྷ་སྦྱིན་ལྕགས་སྒྲོག་གིས་བཅིངས་པ་དང་ཐར་པ་བཞིན་ལ། རྩོད་པའི་གཞིར་གྱུར་པ་བཅིངས་པ་དང་ཐར་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱང་བཅིངས་པ་དང་། ཐར་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་རང་བཞིན་གྱི་གཏན་ཚིགས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་བྱེད་པ་པོ་ལ་གཞི་གཅིག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལ་ཡང་སྦྱོར་བ་རྟག་པར་བྱའོ་ཞེས་ཟེར་རོ། །

There is no postulating that Devadatta is bound and later Yajñadatta is liberated. Nor is there the experiencing by one of the fruit of karma done by another. Because it would become an extreme absurdity, and it would logically follow that what is done is wasted and one meets with what is not done; thus, because that which is the moment of consciousness imputed as the agent has no connection with the fruit, there is the fault of what is done being wasted; and because precisely that which is not the agent is connected with the fruit, there also becomes the fault of meeting with what is not done. Remembering and so forth are also not renowned in the world as having different bases. If one asks, 'Well then, how is it?', they have precisely a single basis: what is experienced by the mind of Devadatta is not remembered or recognized by the mind of Yajñadatta, but it is renowned that whatever experiences it, that itself remembers and recognizes. Therefore, there exists a single person who follows along all occasions. The syllogism is: 'Whatever are bound and liberated, those have a single basis, like for example Devadatta being bound by iron fetters and being liberated; and both being bound and being liberated, which have become the basis of debate, are also being bound and being liberated'—this is a reason of nature. Similarly, for establishing the agent as having precisely a single basis, one should also investigate the syllogism,' they say.

source: ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ས་བོན་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ནུས་པ་ངེས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་རྒྱུའི་ནུས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལ་ཡང་དག་གང་གིས་ན་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དངོས་པོ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ནི་གཅིག་པུ་རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ་ནི་གང་ཡང་མེད་དེ། གནས་སྐབས་གཞན་དུ་སྣང་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུ་འདི་ལ་ཡང་དེ་དང་འདྲ་བར་འགྱུར་ན། བདག་ཏུ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པ་འདིས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། བདག་ལ་ཡང་བརྟགས་ཏེ་བྱེད་པ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ནི་རྒྱུའོ། །ཟབ་མོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ནི་འབྲས་བུའོ་ཞེས་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དངོས་པོ་གདོན་མི་ཟ་བར་ཁས་བླང་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ་གནས་སྐབས་དེ་གཉིས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པའམ། གཅིག་ལ་གཅིག་ཕན་འདོགས་པ་མེད་པ་ན་ནམ་མཁའ་དང་འདྲ་བར་གྱུར་པས་ཟ་བ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འགྲུབ་པར་ཡང་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། ནུས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པར་ཁས་བླང་བར་བྱ་སྟེ། འདི་ལྟར་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་དང་འབྲེལ་པས་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་གྱི་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་བས་ན་དགེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུར་གྱུར་པ་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡོངས་སུ་སྣང་བ་དག་ཁོ་ན་བྱེད་པ་པོ་དང་ཟ་བ་པོ་ཡིན་ན་བལྟར་མི་སྣང་བའི་ངོ་བོ་བདག་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། རྗེས་སུ་དཔག་པས་བདག་དེ་མ་གྲུབ་ཏུ་ཆུག་ཀྱང་། འོན་ཀྱང་སྔར་ཤེས་པའི་མངོན་སུམ་གྱི་ཡུལ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་མངོན་སུམ་གྱིས་བདག་གྲུབ་པོ་ཞེ་ན། དེ་ཡང་རིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེར་འཁྲུལ་པའི་ཕྱིར་དང་། རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཕྱིར་དང་ཤེས་པ་མངོན་སུམ་ཉིད་དུ་མི་འགྲུབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །
translation: Nor is it an extreme absurdity, because the capabilities of causes are individually determined, just as the capabilities of seeds and so forth are determined. Regarding that, whatever single one follows along by which the entities of cause and fruit would truly become individually determined does not exist at all, because they appear in different occasions. If, regarding this continuum of a sentient being also, it becomes similar to that, what is the use of this completely imputed self? Even if one imputes a self, one must undoubtedly accept the entities of cause and fruit, saying: 'Whatever is the occasion of being an agent and so forth is the cause; whatever is the occasion of being an enjoyer and so forth is the fruit.' If it were not so, and there were no arising in those two occasions, or no benefiting of one by the other, then because it would become like space, how could being an enjoyer and so forth also be established? One must accept that capabilities are individually determined: thus, because it is connected with an individually determined nature, happiness and so forth will arise, but not for all. Therefore, if precisely those which appear completely as causes and fruits, virtue and so forth, are the agent and the enjoyer, what is the use of completely imputing a self whose nature does not appear to be seen? If one says, 'Even if one grants that that self is not established by inference, nevertheless, because it is an object of previously known direct perception, the self is established by direct perception,' that too is not logical, because of being mistaken regarding that, because of being accompanied by conceptualization, and because the cognition is not established as direct perception itself.

There is no postulating that Devadatta is bound and later Yajñadatta is liberated. Nor is there the experiencing by one of the fruit of karma done by another. Because it would become an extreme absurdity, and it would logically follow that what is done is wasted and one meets with what is not done; thus, because that which is the moment of consciousness imputed as the agent has no connection with the fruit, there is the fault of what is done being wasted; and because precisely that which is not the agent is connected with the fruit, there also becomes the fault of meeting with what is not done. Remembering and so forth are also not renowned in the world as having different bases. If one asks, 'Well then, how is it?', they have precisely a single basis: what is experienced by the mind of Devadatta is not remembered or recognized by the mind of Yajñadatta, but it is renowned that whatever experiences it, that itself remembers and recognizes. Therefore, there exists a single person who follows along all occasions. The syllogism is: 'Whatever are bound and liberated, those have a single basis, like for example Devadatta being bound by iron fetters and being liberated; and both being bound and being liberated, which have become the basis of debate, are also being bound and being liberated'—this is a reason of nature. Similarly, for establishing the agent as having precisely a single basis, one should also investigate the syllogism,' they say.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: When it appears to the I-cognition, by what would it become direct perception? A self that is single, permanent, and all-pervasive, such as what is imputed from one's own tenet system, is not observed. Undoubtedly it should be known in that way. If it were not so, and if the I-cognition were to become direct perception, then at that time proponents would not dispute regarding the self that has become the object, because, being accompanied by conceptualization, grasping at 'I' would have become of a determinate nature. This is because there is no superimposition regarding what has been made an object by determination. Therefore, because one is deceived by the arising of one similar thing after another, and because, by the force of habituation since beginningless time, one superimposes a singleness upon the individually determined aggregates of form and so forth and thus completely engages the other, one cognizes thinking 'I', because in that cognition those very [aggregates], form and so forth, appear. If one asks, 'If this grasping at 'I' possesses the body as its object, how would it grasp at a mere difference, saying 'my body'?' that is also similar for that which possesses the self as its focal object: if this grasping at 'I' possesses a self as its object, then at that time how would one think 'my self'? If one says, 'Even though there is no difference in the entity itself, because one wishes to cognize merely that by eliminating other differences, just like the expression 'the body of a pestle', there is no contradiction because it grasps by imputing a difference,' that is also similar for that which possesses the body as its focal object.

Nor is it an extreme absurdity, because the capabilities of causes are individually determined, just as the capabilities of seeds and so forth are determined. Regarding that, whatever single one follows along by which the entities of cause and fruit would truly become individually determined does not exist at all, because they appear in different occasions. If, regarding this continuum of a sentient being also, it becomes similar to that, what is the use of this completely imputed self? Even if one imputes a self, one must undoubtedly accept the entities of cause and fruit, saying: 'Whatever is the occasion of being an agent and so forth is the cause; whatever is the occasion of being an enjoyer and so forth is the fruit.' If it were not so, and there were no arising in those two occasions, or no benefiting of one by the other, then because it would become like space, how could being an enjoyer and so forth also be established? One must accept that capabilities are individually determined: thus, because it is connected with an individually determined nature, happiness and so forth will arise, but not for all. Therefore, if precisely those which appear completely as causes and fruits, virtue and so forth, are the agent and the enjoyer, what is the use of completely imputing a self whose nature does not appear to be seen? If one says, 'Even if one grants that that self is not established by inference, nevertheless, because it is an object of previously known direct perception, the self is established by direct perception,' that too is not logical, because of being mistaken regarding that, because of being accompanied by conceptualization, and because the cognition is not established as direct perception itself.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: Possessing the self as its object also contradicts arising by degrees, and will be explained below. Nor is grasping at 'I' itself the self, nor is it possible to state that its objects, form and so forth, are the self, because those have dissimilar characteristics from it. Because those are observed exactly in a sequence, they do not exist as a single nature or as a sovereign one. For that very reason, it is explained: 'The divine self itself is not the characteristic of the self; because the attendants are dissimilar, it is not.' If one designates it as a name, since that is asserted, there is no dispute whatsoever regarding this. Therefore, there is not even the slightest valid cognition that establishes the self. That there is no valid cognition other than direct perception and inference has been analyzed elsewhere. The invalidating valid cognition is also observed only as an eliminator: thus, if the self were not other than the aggregates, then at that time it would become momentary like the aggregates, or else the aggregates would become permanent like the self, because of being undifferentiated from it. Its absurdly becoming a multiplicity like the aggregates would also become difficult to reverse. Therefore, it is asserted that the name 'self' applies only to the aggregates, for there is no dispute regarding a name. However, if one asserts the aggregates as different from the self, then at that time, because there is no connection with happiness and so forth, it would not be established as an enjoyer and so forth.

Regarding that, if here one establishes a person and a sovereign one that is ultimate, permanent, and single, then at that time, because a connection together between such a person and the reason is not established anywhere, it is inconclusive. Because all formations are momentary, Devadatta and so forth are not established in the nature of being permanent and single, so the example also lacks what is to be established. For that very reason, the reason is contradictory, because it is connected with the opposite of that. However, if for some reason one establishes merely that they have a single basis, at that time it is establishing what is already established, for by that, too, it is indeed asserted that being bound and so forth have a single basis due to existing in a single continuum. Thus, at whatever time, in whatever continuum, those which have become cause and fruit, ignorance and so forth, arise continuously without the continuum being interrupted, at that time one designates it as 'being bound'. Moreover, when the noble path arises in that very [continuum] by degrees through hearing and so forth, and through the cessation of ignorance and so forth a transformation of basis occurs, it is designated as 'being liberated', but there is no establishing that those two possess an object that is an ultimate, permanent, single entity, because worldly being bound and being liberated are also similar to that. In whatever continuum a virtuous or non-virtuous mind and experience have arisen, in that very [continuum] at another time, in dependence upon the continuum having completely ripened—like the complete ripening of the continuum of a mātuluṅga and so forth that has been smeared with the juice of lac and so forth—because fruits such as happiness, suffering, and remembering appear to arise, virtue and so forth are renowned as having a single basis; but there is not any single agent, enjoyer, or rememberer, because all these imputed conventions are thoroughly distinguished merely by cause and fruit.

ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ས་བོན་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ནུས་པ་ངེས་པ་བཞིན་དུ་རྒྱུའི་ནུས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལ་ཡང་དག་གང་གིས་ན་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དངོས་པོ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ནི་གཅིག་པུ་རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ་ནི་གང་ཡང་མེད་དེ། གནས་སྐབས་གཞན་དུ་སྣང་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུ་འདི་ལ་ཡང་དེ་དང་འདྲ་བར་འགྱུར་ན། བདག་ཏུ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པ་འདིས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། བདག་ལ་ཡང་བརྟགས་ཏེ་བྱེད་པ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ནི་རྒྱུའོ། །ཟབ་མོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་ནི་འབྲས་བུའོ་ཞེས་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དངོས་པོ་གདོན་མི་ཟ་བར་ཁས་བླང་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ་གནས་སྐབས་དེ་གཉིས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པའམ། གཅིག་ལ་གཅིག་ཕན་འདོགས་པ་མེད་པ་ན་ནམ་མཁའ་དང་འདྲ་བར་གྱུར་པས་ཟ་བ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འགྲུབ་པར་ཡང་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། ནུས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པར་ཁས་བླང་བར་བྱ་སྟེ། འདི་ལྟར་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་དང་འབྲེལ་པས་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་གྱི་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་བས་ན་དགེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུར་གྱུར་པ་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡོངས་སུ་སྣང་བ་དག་ཁོ་ན་བྱེད་པ་པོ་དང་ཟ་བ་པོ་ཡིན་ན་བལྟར་མི་སྣང་བའི་ངོ་བོ་བདག་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། རྗེས་སུ་དཔག་པས་བདག་དེ་མ་གྲུབ་ཏུ་ཆུག་ཀྱང་། འོན་ཀྱང་སྔར་ཤེས་པའི་མངོན་སུམ་གྱི་ཡུལ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་མངོན་སུམ་གྱིས་བདག་གྲུབ་པོ་ཞེ་ན། དེ་ཡང་རིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེར་འཁྲུལ་པའི་ཕྱིར་དང་། རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཕྱིར་དང་ཤེས་པ་མངོན་སུམ་ཉིད་དུ་མི་འགྲུབ་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །

Nor is it an extreme absurdity, because the capabilities of causes are individually determined, just as the capabilities of seeds and so forth are determined. Regarding that, whatever single one follows along by which the entities of cause and fruit would truly become individually determined does not exist at all, because they appear in different occasions. If, regarding this continuum of a sentient being also, it becomes similar to that, what is the use of this completely imputed self? Even if one imputes a self, one must undoubtedly accept the entities of cause and fruit, saying: 'Whatever is the occasion of being an agent and so forth is the cause; whatever is the occasion of being an enjoyer and so forth is the fruit.' If it were not so, and there were no arising in those two occasions, or no benefiting of one by the other, then because it would become like space, how could being an enjoyer and so forth also be established? One must accept that capabilities are individually determined: thus, because it is connected with an individually determined nature, happiness and so forth will arise, but not for all. Therefore, if precisely those which appear completely as causes and fruits, virtue and so forth, are the agent and the enjoyer, what is the use of completely imputing a self whose nature does not appear to be seen? If one says, 'Even if one grants that that self is not established by inference, nevertheless, because it is an object of previously known direct perception, the self is established by direct perception,' that too is not logical, because of being mistaken regarding that, because of being accompanied by conceptualization, and because the cognition is not established as direct perception itself.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
source: སྦྱོར་བ་ནི་གང་ཞིག་བདེ་བ་དང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་ནི་བྱེད་པ་པོ་འམ་ཟ་བ་པོ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། གྲོལ་བར་བྱེད་པའམ་འཁོར་བར་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན་པར་ཡང་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མོ་གཤམ་གྱི་བུ་བཞིན་ལ། བདག་ཀྱང་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་གང་ཡང་མེད་པས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་ཁྱབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་ནི་མི་དམིགས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །གཏན་ཚིགས་མ་གྲུབ་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། འདི་ལྟར་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ན་གཞི་དང་གནས་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ། ལྡན་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ། རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ་ཕྱོགས་གསུམ་དུ་འགྱུར་གྲང་ན། རེ་ཞིག་ཕྱོགས་དང་པོ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ཅི་ཡང་མི་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འདི་ལྟར་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ཆོས་ཆུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་གེགས་བྱེད་པས་གཞིར་རྣམ་པར་གཞག་ན། བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་ནི་ལུས་མེད་པས་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་མི་སྲིད་པའི་ཕྱིར་བདག་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱེད་ན་གཞིར་འགྱུར། གནས་པར་བྱེད་པས་ཀྱང་གཞི་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། གནས་པ་དང་གནས་པ་པོ་ཐ་མི་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་ཉིད་བྱེད་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེ་ཡང་དགག་པར་བྱའོ། །གནས་པ་དང་ཐ་དད་ན་ཡང་དེ་གནས་པ་པོ་དེ་ལ་ཕན་འདོགས་པར་བྱེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་པ་ཉིད་དེ། གནས་པ་དོན་གཞན་དུ་གྱུར་པ་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལ་ནི་གནས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་མཐུ་ཡང་མེད་དེ། ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་མཐུ་མེད་པར་གསལ་བར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །
translation: The syllogism is: whatever is unconnected with happiness, suffering, and so forth is not an agent or an enjoyer, nor is it logical to be one who liberates or one who cycles, like the son of a barren woman, for instance. Saying, 'Because the self, too, lacks any connection whatsoever with actions and so forth' is the non-observation of a pervader. The reason is also not unestablished. Thus, if there were a connection with happiness and so forth, it would be [one of] three alternatives: the characteristic of support and supported, or the characteristic of possession, or the characteristic of cause and effect. First, it is not the first alternative, because it does not do anything at all. Thus, if something is posited as a support by obstructing the downward movement of phenomena that move downward, such as water, then because happiness and so forth are bodiless and thus it is impossible for them to move downward, by doing what would the self become a support? Nor is it a support by causing abiding, because, since the abiding and the abider are undifferentiated, it would produce that very thing, and that also should be refuted. Even if it were different from the abiding, it would definitely not benefit that abider, because it would produce an abiding that has become another entity. It also lacks the power to generate an abiding in it, because it will be clarified that it lacks power regarding everything.

When it appears to the I-cognition, by what would it become direct perception? A self that is single, permanent, and all-pervasive, such as what is imputed from one's own tenet system, is not observed. Undoubtedly it should be known in that way. If it were not so, and if the I-cognition were to become direct perception, then at that time proponents would not dispute regarding the self that has become the object, because, being accompanied by conceptualization, grasping at 'I' would have become of a determinate nature. This is because there is no superimposition regarding what has been made an object by determination. Therefore, because one is deceived by the arising of one similar thing after another, and because, by the force of habituation since beginningless time, one superimposes a singleness upon the individually determined aggregates of form and so forth and thus completely engages the other, one cognizes thinking 'I', because in that cognition those very [aggregates], form and so forth, appear. If one asks, 'If this grasping at 'I' possesses the body as its object, how would it grasp at a mere difference, saying 'my body'?' that is also similar for that which possesses the self as its focal object: if this grasping at 'I' possesses a self as its object, then at that time how would one think 'my self'? If one says, 'Even though there is no difference in the entity itself, because one wishes to cognize merely that by eliminating other differences, just like the expression 'the body of a pestle', there is no contradiction because it grasps by imputing a difference,' that is also similar for that which possesses the body as its focal object.

བདག་གི་ཡུལ་ཅན་ཡང་རིམ་གྱིས་འབྱུང་བ་དང་འགལ་ཏེ་འོག་ནས་བཤད་དོ། །ངར་འཛིན་པ་ཁོ་ན་ཡང་བདག་མ་ཡིན་ལ་དེའི་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་བདག་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པར་ཡང་མི་ནུས་ཏེ། དེ་དག་དེ་དང་མཚན་ཉིད་མི་འདྲ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་དག་ནི་རིམ་ཉིད་དུ་དམིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་གཅིག་པུའི་ངོ་བོའམ་རང་དབང་ཅན་དུ་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར། བདག་ལྷ་ཉིད་ནི་བདག་གི་མཚན་ཉིད་མིན། ཉེ་གནས་མི་འདྲ་བས་ན་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བཤད་དོ། །མིང་དུ་འདོགས་ན་ནི་འདོད་པས་འདི་ལ་བརྩད་པ་ཅི་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བདག་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚད་མ་ཆུང་ཟད་ཙམ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྗེས་སུ་དཔག་པ་ལས་མ་གཏོགས་པའི་ཚད་མ་ནི་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་ཕྱོགས་གཞན་དུ་དཔྱད་ཟིན་ཏོ། །གནོད་པ་ཅན་གྱི་ཚད་མ་ཡང་བསལ་བ་ཁོ་ནར་དམིགས་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་གལ་ཏེ་བདག་ཕུང་པོ་དག་ལས་གཞན་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་སྐད་ཅིག་པར་འགྱུར་བའམ། ཡང་ན་བདག་བཞིན་དུ་ཕུང་པོ་རྟག་པ་དག་ཏུ་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེ་དང་ཐ་མི་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་དུ་མ་ཉིད་དུ་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་ཡང་བཟློག་དཀའ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་བས་ན་ཕུང་པོ་རྣམས་ཁོ་ན་ལ་བདག་ཅེས་མིང་འདོད་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། མིང་ལ་ནི་བརྩད་པ་མེད་དོ། །འོན་ཏེ་ཕུང་པོ་བདག་དང་ཐ་དད་པར་འདོན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་པས་དེ་ཟ་བ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པར་མི་འགྲུབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །

Possessing the self as its object also contradicts arising by degrees, and will be explained below. Nor is grasping at 'I' itself the self, nor is it possible to state that its objects, form and so forth, are the self, because those have dissimilar characteristics from it. Because those are observed exactly in a sequence, they do not exist as a single nature or as a sovereign one. For that very reason, it is explained: 'The divine self itself is not the characteristic of the self; because the attendants are dissimilar, it is not.' If one designates it as a name, since that is asserted, there is no dispute whatsoever regarding this. Therefore, there is not even the slightest valid cognition that establishes the self. That there is no valid cognition other than direct perception and inference has been analyzed elsewhere. The invalidating valid cognition is also observed only as an eliminator: thus, if the self were not other than the aggregates, then at that time it would become momentary like the aggregates, or else the aggregates would become permanent like the self, because of being undifferentiated from it. Its absurdly becoming a multiplicity like the aggregates would also become difficult to reverse. Therefore, it is asserted that the name 'self' applies only to the aggregates, for there is no dispute regarding a name. However, if one asserts the aggregates as different from the self, then at that time, because there is no connection with happiness and so forth, it would not be established as an enjoyer and so forth.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: For a nature that is changeable by itself, there is nothing whatsoever that causes it to abide, because it [already] abides. If it were not so, it would only be destroyed by it, and it would not be made to abide. For an unchangeable nature, too, what is the use of something that causes it to abide, because it abides as a stable nature by itself? Therefore, because it does not do anything, a connection of possession is also unsuitable, because it would be extremely absurd. If it were so, everything would become the cause of everything's possession. It is illogical for another entity to possess another entity, because everything abides in itself, like an iron peg. Furthermore, if by the force of possession the self were to become happy or suffering, then at that time that possession would be single; because there is no difference, it would not become connected with an individually determined nature of happiness and so forth. Therefore, by happiness and so forth, the single self, too, would not entirely become happiness itself or suffering itself. If one asserts determination by the force of the unseen, if it is determined by that alone, what is the use of thoroughly imputing possession? Because it lacks power anywhere. Regarding imputing a difference because the connected [things] are different, if ultimately the nature of entities is not different, by what would there become a difference of causal functioning that depends on a difference of nature? Therefore, this connection is thoroughly conceptualized only by bad intellects.

When it appears to the I-cognition, by what would it become direct perception? A self that is single, permanent, and all-pervasive, such as what is imputed from one's own tenet system, is not observed. Undoubtedly it should be known in that way. If it were not so, and if the I-cognition were to become direct perception, then at that time proponents would not dispute regarding the self that has become the object, because, being accompanied by conceptualization, grasping at 'I' would have become of a determinate nature. This is because there is no superimposition regarding what has been made an object by determination. Therefore, because one is deceived by the arising of one similar thing after another, and because, by the force of habituation since beginningless time, one superimposes a singleness upon the individually determined aggregates of form and so forth and thus completely engages the other, one cognizes thinking 'I', because in that cognition those very [aggregates], form and so forth, appear. If one asks, 'If this grasping at 'I' possesses the body as its object, how would it grasp at a mere difference, saying 'my body'?' that is also similar for that which possesses the self as its focal object: if this grasping at 'I' possesses a self as its object, then at that time how would one think 'my self'? If one says, 'Even though there is no difference in the entity itself, because one wishes to cognize merely that by eliminating other differences, just like the expression 'the body of a pestle', there is no contradiction because it grasps by imputing a difference,' that is also similar for that which possesses the body as its focal object.

བདག་གི་ཡུལ་ཅན་ཡང་རིམ་གྱིས་འབྱུང་བ་དང་འགལ་ཏེ་འོག་ནས་བཤད་དོ། །ངར་འཛིན་པ་ཁོ་ན་ཡང་བདག་མ་ཡིན་ལ་དེའི་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་བདག་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པར་ཡང་མི་ནུས་ཏེ། དེ་དག་དེ་དང་མཚན་ཉིད་མི་འདྲ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་དག་ནི་རིམ་ཉིད་དུ་དམིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་གཅིག་པུའི་ངོ་བོའམ་རང་དབང་ཅན་དུ་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར། བདག་ལྷ་ཉིད་ནི་བདག་གི་མཚན་ཉིད་མིན། ཉེ་གནས་མི་འདྲ་བས་ན་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བཤད་དོ། །མིང་དུ་འདོགས་ན་ནི་འདོད་པས་འདི་ལ་བརྩད་པ་ཅི་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བདག་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚད་མ་ཆུང་ཟད་ཙམ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྗེས་སུ་དཔག་པ་ལས་མ་གཏོགས་པའི་ཚད་མ་ནི་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་ཕྱོགས་གཞན་དུ་དཔྱད་ཟིན་ཏོ། །གནོད་པ་ཅན་གྱི་ཚད་མ་ཡང་བསལ་བ་ཁོ་ནར་དམིགས་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་གལ་ཏེ་བདག་ཕུང་པོ་དག་ལས་གཞན་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་སྐད་ཅིག་པར་འགྱུར་བའམ། ཡང་ན་བདག་བཞིན་དུ་ཕུང་པོ་རྟག་པ་དག་ཏུ་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེ་དང་ཐ་མི་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་དུ་མ་ཉིད་དུ་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་ཡང་བཟློག་དཀའ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་བས་ན་ཕུང་པོ་རྣམས་ཁོ་ན་ལ་བདག་ཅེས་མིང་འདོད་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། མིང་ལ་ནི་བརྩད་པ་མེད་དོ། །འོན་ཏེ་ཕུང་པོ་བདག་དང་ཐ་དད་པར་འདོན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་པས་དེ་ཟ་བ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པར་མི་འགྲུབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །

Possessing the self as its object also contradicts arising by degrees, and will be explained below. Nor is grasping at 'I' itself the self, nor is it possible to state that its objects, form and so forth, are the self, because those have dissimilar characteristics from it. Because those are observed exactly in a sequence, they do not exist as a single nature or as a sovereign one. For that very reason, it is explained: 'The divine self itself is not the characteristic of the self; because the attendants are dissimilar, it is not.' If one designates it as a name, since that is asserted, there is no dispute whatsoever regarding this. Therefore, there is not even the slightest valid cognition that establishes the self. That there is no valid cognition other than direct perception and inference has been analyzed elsewhere. The invalidating valid cognition is also observed only as an eliminator: thus, if the self were not other than the aggregates, then at that time it would become momentary like the aggregates, or else the aggregates would become permanent like the self, because of being undifferentiated from it. Its absurdly becoming a multiplicity like the aggregates would also become difficult to reverse. Therefore, it is asserted that the name 'self' applies only to the aggregates, for there is no dispute regarding a name. However, if one asserts the aggregates as different from the self, then at that time, because there is no connection with happiness and so forth, it would not be established as an enjoyer and so forth.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: Nor is it a connection through cause and effect, because happiness and so forth are seen to arise by degrees. It is illogical for an effect whose causes are not incomplete to sometimes arise or not arise, because there is no difference. For the self, which cannot be differentiated by others or possesses independent power, there is no dependence on a cooperative cause, by which it would arise by degrees in dependence on a cooperative cause. Therefore, if it is bound by being the cause that generates suffering, then at that time it would be bound at all times and would not become liberated, because it would not thoroughly abandon such a kind of nature. If it thoroughly abandons it, how would it become permanent? However, if it is liberated by being the cause that generates a state without suffering, then at that time it would exactly become liberated; if it is never bound, then at that time how could one thoroughly impute a bondage and liberation that have a basis? Likewise, if it is an agent by performing the characteristic of intention and so forth or by being capable of generating them, then at that time it would become an agent at all times, so how would it become an enjoyer? But if it is an enjoyer by being the cause that generates happiness and so forth, then at that time it would exactly become an enjoyer, so how would it become an agent? That which is thoroughly conceptualized by the Sāṃkhyas, unchanging like space due to happiness and so forth, is also not endowed with the logic to be an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd.

བདག་གི་ཡུལ་ཅན་ཡང་རིམ་གྱིས་འབྱུང་བ་དང་འགལ་ཏེ་འོག་ནས་བཤད་དོ། །ངར་འཛིན་པ་ཁོ་ན་ཡང་བདག་མ་ཡིན་ལ་དེའི་ཡུལ་གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་བདག་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པར་ཡང་མི་ནུས་ཏེ། དེ་དག་དེ་དང་མཚན་ཉིད་མི་འདྲ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་དག་ནི་རིམ་ཉིད་དུ་དམིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་གཅིག་པུའི་ངོ་བོའམ་རང་དབང་ཅན་དུ་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར། བདག་ལྷ་ཉིད་ནི་བདག་གི་མཚན་ཉིད་མིན། ཉེ་གནས་མི་འདྲ་བས་ན་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བཤད་དོ། །མིང་དུ་འདོགས་ན་ནི་འདོད་པས་འདི་ལ་བརྩད་པ་ཅི་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བདག་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཚད་མ་ཆུང་ཟད་ཙམ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྗེས་སུ་དཔག་པ་ལས་མ་གཏོགས་པའི་ཚད་མ་ནི་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་ཕྱོགས་གཞན་དུ་དཔྱད་ཟིན་ཏོ། །གནོད་པ་ཅན་གྱི་ཚད་མ་ཡང་བསལ་བ་ཁོ་ནར་དམིགས་ཏེ། དེ་ལྟར་གལ་ཏེ་བདག་ཕུང་པོ་དག་ལས་གཞན་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་སྐད་ཅིག་པར་འགྱུར་བའམ། ཡང་ན་བདག་བཞིན་དུ་ཕུང་པོ་རྟག་པ་དག་ཏུ་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེ་དང་ཐ་མི་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཕུང་པོ་བཞིན་དུ་དུ་མ་ཉིད་དུ་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་ཡང་བཟློག་དཀའ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེ་བས་ན་ཕུང་པོ་རྣམས་ཁོ་ན་ལ་བདག་ཅེས་མིང་འདོད་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། མིང་ལ་ནི་བརྩད་པ་མེད་དོ། །འོན་ཏེ་ཕུང་པོ་བདག་དང་ཐ་དད་པར་འདོན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་པས་དེ་ཟ་བ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པར་མི་འགྲུབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །

Possessing the self as its object also contradicts arising by degrees, and will be explained below. Nor is grasping at 'I' itself the self, nor is it possible to state that its objects, form and so forth, are the self, because those have dissimilar characteristics from it. Because those are observed exactly in a sequence, they do not exist as a single nature or as a sovereign one. For that very reason, it is explained: 'The divine self itself is not the characteristic of the self; because the attendants are dissimilar, it is not.' If one designates it as a name, since that is asserted, there is no dispute whatsoever regarding this. Therefore, there is not even the slightest valid cognition that establishes the self. That there is no valid cognition other than direct perception and inference has been analyzed elsewhere. The invalidating valid cognition is also observed only as an eliminator: thus, if the self were not other than the aggregates, then at that time it would become momentary like the aggregates, or else the aggregates would become permanent like the self, because of being undifferentiated from it. Its absurdly becoming a multiplicity like the aggregates would also become difficult to reverse. Therefore, it is asserted that the name 'self' applies only to the aggregates, for there is no dispute regarding a name. However, if one asserts the aggregates as different from the self, then at that time, because there is no connection with happiness and so forth, it would not be established as an enjoyer and so forth.

སྦྱོར་བ་ནི་གང་ཞིག་བདེ་བ་དང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་མེད་པ་དེ་ནི་བྱེད་པ་པོ་འམ་ཟ་བ་པོ་མ་ཡིན་ལ། གྲོལ་བར་བྱེད་པའམ་འཁོར་བར་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན་པར་ཡང་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། དཔེར་ན་མོ་གཤམ་གྱི་བུ་བཞིན་ལ། བདག་ཀྱང་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་གང་ཡང་མེད་པས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་ཁྱབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་ནི་མི་དམིགས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ། །གཏན་ཚིགས་མ་གྲུབ་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། འདི་ལྟར་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ན་གཞི་དང་གནས་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ། ལྡན་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ། རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དམ་ཕྱོགས་གསུམ་དུ་འགྱུར་གྲང་ན། རེ་ཞིག་ཕྱོགས་དང་པོ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ཅི་ཡང་མི་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འདི་ལྟར་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ཆོས་ཆུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བའི་གེགས་བྱེད་པས་གཞིར་རྣམ་པར་གཞག་ན། བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་ནི་ལུས་མེད་པས་འོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་མི་སྲིད་པའི་ཕྱིར་བདག་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱེད་ན་གཞིར་འགྱུར། གནས་པར་བྱེད་པས་ཀྱང་གཞི་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། གནས་པ་དང་གནས་པ་པོ་ཐ་མི་དད་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་ཉིད་བྱེད་པར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེ་ཡང་དགག་པར་བྱའོ། །གནས་པ་དང་ཐ་དད་ན་ཡང་དེ་གནས་པ་པོ་དེ་ལ་ཕན་འདོགས་པར་བྱེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་པ་ཉིད་དེ། གནས་པ་དོན་གཞན་དུ་གྱུར་པ་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལ་ནི་གནས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་མཐུ་ཡང་མེད་དེ། ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་མཐུ་མེད་པར་གསལ་བར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །

The syllogism is: whatever is unconnected with happiness, suffering, and so forth is not an agent or an enjoyer, nor is it logical to be one who liberates or one who cycles, like the son of a barren woman, for instance. Saying, 'Because the self, too, lacks any connection whatsoever with actions and so forth' is the non-observation of a pervader. The reason is also not unestablished. Thus, if there were a connection with happiness and so forth, it would be [one of] three alternatives: the characteristic of support and supported, or the characteristic of possession, or the characteristic of cause and effect. First, it is not the first alternative, because it does not do anything at all. Thus, if something is posited as a support by obstructing the downward movement of phenomena that move downward, such as water, then because happiness and so forth are bodiless and thus it is impossible for them to move downward, by doing what would the self become a support? Nor is it a support by causing abiding, because, since the abiding and the abider are undifferentiated, it would produce that very thing, and that also should be refuted. Even if it were different from the abiding, it would definitely not benefit that abider, because it would produce an abiding that has become another entity. It also lacks the power to generate an abiding in it, because it will be clarified that it lacks power regarding everything.

བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་འགྱུར་བའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ལ་ནི་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡང་མེད་དེ། དེ་ནི་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ན་དེས་དེ་གཞིག་པ་ཁོ་ནར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། གནས་པར་བྱས་པ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །མི་འགྱུར་བའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ལ་ཡང་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ་སྟེ། བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བརྟན་པའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་དུ་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་ཅི་ཡང་མི་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་ལྡན་པའི་འབྲེལ་པ་ཡང་མི་རུང་སྟེ། ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་ན་ནི་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱང་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་ལྡན་པ་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དོན་གཞན་དང་དོན་གཞན་དུ་ལྡན་པར་ནི་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། ལྕགས་ཀྱི་ཐུར་མ་བཞིན་དུ་ཐམས་ཅད་བདག་ཉིད་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །གཞན་ཡང་གལ་ཏེ་ལྡན་པའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་བདག་བདེ་བའམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བར་གྱུར་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ལྡན་པ་དེ་གཅིག་པུ་སྟེ། བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་ཅན་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་བདག་གཅིག་པུ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་ཀྱང་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བ་ཉིད་དམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཉིད་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་རོ། །མི་མཐོང་བའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་ངེས་པའི་ཁས་ལེན་ན་ནི་དེ་ཁོ་ནས་ངེས་པ་ཡིན་ན་ལྡན་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། དེ་ནི་གང་དུ་ཡང་མཐུ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འབྲེལ་པ་ཅན་ཐ་དད་པས་ཐ་དད་པར་འདོགས་པ་ལ་ཡང་དོན་དམ་པར་ནི་དངོས་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་ཐ་དད་པ་མེད་ན། གང་གིས་རང་བཞིན་ཐ་དད་པ་ལ་རག་ལུས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པའི་ཐ་དད་པར་འགྱུར། དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་འབྲེལ་པ་འདི་ནི་བློ་གྲོས་ངན་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པ་ཁོ་ནའོ། །

For a nature that is changeable by itself, there is nothing whatsoever that causes it to abide, because it [already] abides. If it were not so, it would only be destroyed by it, and it would not be made to abide. For an unchangeable nature, too, what is the use of something that causes it to abide, because it abides as a stable nature by itself? Therefore, because it does not do anything, a connection of possession is also unsuitable, because it would be extremely absurd. If it were so, everything would become the cause of everything's possession. It is illogical for another entity to possess another entity, because everything abides in itself, like an iron peg. Furthermore, if by the force of possession the self were to become happy or suffering, then at that time that possession would be single; because there is no difference, it would not become connected with an individually determined nature of happiness and so forth. Therefore, by happiness and so forth, the single self, too, would not entirely become happiness itself or suffering itself. If one asserts determination by the force of the unseen, if it is determined by that alone, what is the use of thoroughly imputing possession? Because it lacks power anywhere. Regarding imputing a difference because the connected [things] are different, if ultimately the nature of entities is not different, by what would there become a difference of causal functioning that depends on a difference of nature? Therefore, this connection is thoroughly conceptualized only by bad intellects.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: If it changes, permanence itself degenerates. Merely by being a cause it does not become an agent and an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd. Likewise, one should apply that a rememberer and so forth are also unsuitable to possess that as a basis. Therefore, it is only in the position that advocates selflessness that the presentation of liberation, bondage, and so forth is endowed with logic, because that presentation is thoroughly differentiated merely by the difference of cause and effect. That entity of cause and effect also is possible only for the impermanent, but not for the permanent, because they lack the power to generate any effect by degrees, just as explained before. Nor simultaneously, because the nature of the power to generate such a kind of effect follows again, and thus it is illogical to be separated from generating the effect just like before. If it does not follow, the prior nature would degenerate. Other than successive and simultaneous, there is no other aspect by which it would perform a function, because those two have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. For that very reason, whatever is non-momentary, whatever entities such as space are thoroughly conceptualized by others, all of them are objects of the convention of non-existence because they lack the capacity to perform a function—so the great Buddhist scholars state.

Possessing the self as its object also contradicts arising by degrees, and will be explained below. Nor is grasping at 'I' itself the self, nor is it possible to state that its objects, form and so forth, are the self, because those have dissimilar characteristics from it. Because those are observed exactly in a sequence, they do not exist as a single nature or as a sovereign one. For that very reason, it is explained: 'The divine self itself is not the characteristic of the self; because the attendants are dissimilar, it is not.' If one designates it as a name, since that is asserted, there is no dispute whatsoever regarding this. Therefore, there is not even the slightest valid cognition that establishes the self. That there is no valid cognition other than direct perception and inference has been analyzed elsewhere. The invalidating valid cognition is also observed only as an eliminator: thus, if the self were not other than the aggregates, then at that time it would become momentary like the aggregates, or else the aggregates would become permanent like the self, because of being undifferentiated from it. Its absurdly becoming a multiplicity like the aggregates would also become difficult to reverse. Therefore, it is asserted that the name 'self' applies only to the aggregates, for there is no dispute regarding a name. However, if one asserts the aggregates as different from the self, then at that time, because there is no connection with happiness and so forth, it would not be established as an enjoyer and so forth.

The syllogism is: whatever is unconnected with happiness, suffering, and so forth is not an agent or an enjoyer, nor is it logical to be one who liberates or one who cycles, like the son of a barren woman, for instance. Saying, 'Because the self, too, lacks any connection whatsoever with actions and so forth' is the non-observation of a pervader. The reason is also not unestablished. Thus, if there were a connection with happiness and so forth, it would be [one of] three alternatives: the characteristic of support and supported, or the characteristic of possession, or the characteristic of cause and effect. First, it is not the first alternative, because it does not do anything at all. Thus, if something is posited as a support by obstructing the downward movement of phenomena that move downward, such as water, then because happiness and so forth are bodiless and thus it is impossible for them to move downward, by doing what would the self become a support? Nor is it a support by causing abiding, because, since the abiding and the abider are undifferentiated, it would produce that very thing, and that also should be refuted. Even if it were different from the abiding, it would definitely not benefit that abider, because it would produce an abiding that has become another entity. It also lacks the power to generate an abiding in it, because it will be clarified that it lacks power regarding everything.

For a nature that is changeable by itself, there is nothing whatsoever that causes it to abide, because it [already] abides. If it were not so, it would only be destroyed by it, and it would not be made to abide. For an unchangeable nature, too, what is the use of something that causes it to abide, because it abides as a stable nature by itself? Therefore, because it does not do anything, a connection of possession is also unsuitable, because it would be extremely absurd. If it were so, everything would become the cause of everything's possession. It is illogical for another entity to possess another entity, because everything abides in itself, like an iron peg. Furthermore, if by the force of possession the self were to become happy or suffering, then at that time that possession would be single; because there is no difference, it would not become connected with an individually determined nature of happiness and so forth. Therefore, by happiness and so forth, the single self, too, would not entirely become happiness itself or suffering itself. If one asserts determination by the force of the unseen, if it is determined by that alone, what is the use of thoroughly imputing possession? Because it lacks power anywhere. Regarding imputing a difference because the connected [things] are different, if ultimately the nature of entities is not different, by what would there become a difference of causal functioning that depends on a difference of nature? Therefore, this connection is thoroughly conceptualized only by bad intellects.

heading: སེམས་བསྐྱེད་བཤད་པ།
translation: Imputing the convention of non-existence to a rabbit's horn and so forth is also due to the cause of merely lacking the capacity to perform a function. By implication, the object to which the convention of existence is imputed is exactly what is capable of performing a function, because existence and non-existence have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. If one imputes the name 'entity' even to that which is empty of all capacities of such a kind and is no different from a rabbit's horn and so forth, there is no dispute about names. However, those endowed with understanding of the meaningless assertion state that it is illogical to impute the convention of entity to such a kind of unobservable nature, which is no different from the son of a barren woman and so forth. Therefore, the reason is not unestablished. Because it would absurdly follow that space and so forth are also agents, it is also not inconclusive. Because it exists in what is harmonious with the position, it is also not contradictory. Because there is also no other characteristic of the self, therefore it is similar to the son of a barren woman. As for persons, too, if they perish, it would absurdly follow that they are included exactly within the aggregates, because the aggregates include all conditioned things. But if they do not perish, then at that time, by being dissimilar to the dharmas belonging to the aggregates, they would become exactly another entity from them, and the faults of that have already been stated. Therefore, there is no entity whatsoever that is called inexpressible. Therefore, the lion's roar of the Bhagavan, 'all dharmas are selfless,' terrifies all the herds of tīrthika elephants and is invincible, so there is no need for much.

བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་འགྱུར་བའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ལ་ནི་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡང་མེད་དེ། དེ་ནི་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་མ་ཡིན་ན་དེས་དེ་གཞིག་པ་ཁོ་ནར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། གནས་པར་བྱས་པ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །མི་འགྱུར་བའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ལ་ཡང་གནས་པར་བྱེད་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ་སྟེ། བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བརྟན་པའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་དུ་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་ཅི་ཡང་མི་བྱེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་ལྡན་པའི་འབྲེལ་པ་ཡང་མི་རུང་སྟེ། ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ལྟ་ན་ནི་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱང་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་ལྡན་པ་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དོན་གཞན་དང་དོན་གཞན་དུ་ལྡན་པར་ནི་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། ལྕགས་ཀྱི་ཐུར་མ་བཞིན་དུ་ཐམས་ཅད་བདག་ཉིད་གནས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །གཞན་ཡང་གལ་ཏེ་ལྡན་པའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་བདག་བདེ་བའམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བར་གྱུར་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ལྡན་པ་དེ་གཅིག་པུ་སྟེ། བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་སོ་སོར་ངེས་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་དང་འབྲེལ་པ་ཅན་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེའི་ཕྱིར་བདག་གཅིག་པུ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་ཀྱང་ཐམས་ཅད་བདེ་བ་ཉིད་དམ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཉིད་དུ་མི་འགྱུར་རོ། །མི་མཐོང་བའི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་ངེས་པའི་ཁས་ལེན་ན་ནི་དེ་ཁོ་ནས་ངེས་པ་ཡིན་ན་ལྡན་པ་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པས་ཅི་ཞིག་བྱ། དེ་ནི་གང་དུ་ཡང་མཐུ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འབྲེལ་པ་ཅན་ཐ་དད་པས་ཐ་དད་པར་འདོགས་པ་ལ་ཡང་དོན་དམ་པར་ནི་དངོས་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་ཐ་དད་པ་མེད་ན། གང་གིས་རང་བཞིན་ཐ་དད་པ་ལ་རག་ལུས་པའི་དོན་བྱེད་པའི་ཐ་དད་པར་འགྱུར། དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་འབྲེལ་པ་འདི་ནི་བློ་གྲོས་ངན་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པ་ཁོ་ནའོ། །

For a nature that is changeable by itself, there is nothing whatsoever that causes it to abide, because it [already] abides. If it were not so, it would only be destroyed by it, and it would not be made to abide. For an unchangeable nature, too, what is the use of something that causes it to abide, because it abides as a stable nature by itself? Therefore, because it does not do anything, a connection of possession is also unsuitable, because it would be extremely absurd. If it were so, everything would become the cause of everything's possession. It is illogical for another entity to possess another entity, because everything abides in itself, like an iron peg. Furthermore, if by the force of possession the self were to become happy or suffering, then at that time that possession would be single; because there is no difference, it would not become connected with an individually determined nature of happiness and so forth. Therefore, by happiness and so forth, the single self, too, would not entirely become happiness itself or suffering itself. If one asserts determination by the force of the unseen, if it is determined by that alone, what is the use of thoroughly imputing possession? Because it lacks power anywhere. Regarding imputing a difference because the connected [things] are different, if ultimately the nature of entities is not different, by what would there become a difference of causal functioning that depends on a difference of nature? Therefore, this connection is thoroughly conceptualized only by bad intellects.

རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུས་འབྲེལ་པ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རིམ་གྱིས་འབྱུང་བར་སྣང་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །རྒྱུ་མ་ཚང་བ་མེད་པ་ཅན་གྱི་འབྲས་བུ་ནི་རེས་འགའ་འབྱུང་བའམ་མི་འབྱུང་བར་མི་རིགས་ཏེ། བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །གཞན་དག་གིས་བྱེ་བྲག་ཏུ་བྱར་མི་རུང་བའམ། མཐུ་རག་མ་ལུས་པ་ཅན་གྱི་བདག་ནི་གང་གིས་ན་ལྷན་ཅིག་བྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་ལ་ལྟོས་ནས་རིམ་གྱིས་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་ལྷན་ཅིག་བྱེད་པ་ལ་ལྟོས་པ་ནི་མེད་དོ། །དེས་ན་གལ་ཏེ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་སྐྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུ་ཡིན་པས་དེ་བཅིངས་པ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་བཅིངས་ནས་རྣམ་པར་གྲོལ་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རང་བཞིན་རྣམ་པ་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་ཡོངས་སུ་མི་གཏོང་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཡོངས་སུ་གཏོང་ན་ནི་རྟག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་ག་ལ་འགྱུར། ཅི་སྟེ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མེད་པའི་གནས་སྐབས་སྐྱེས་པའི་རྒྱུ་ཡིན་པས་གྲོལ་བ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་གྲོལ་བ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་ཏེ། ནམ་ཡང་བཅིངས་པར་མི་འགྱུར་ན་དེའི་ཚེ་གཞི་ཅན་གྱི་བཅིངས་པ་དང་གྲོལ་བ་དག་ཏུ་ཇི་ལྟར་རབ་ཏུ་བརྟག །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་གལ་ཏེ་སེམས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་བྱེད་པའམ་བསྐྱེད་ནུས་པས་བྱེད་པ་པོ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་བྱེད་པ་པོར་འགྱུར་གྱི་ཟ་བ་པོར་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར་འོན་ཏེ་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་རྒྱུས་ཟ་བ་པོ་ཡིན་ན་ནི་དེའི་ཚེ་ཟ་བ་པོ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་གྱི་བྱེད་པ་པོར་ཇི་ལྟར་འགྱུར། སེར་སྐྱ་བས་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པའི་བདེ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་འགྱུར་བ་མེད་པ་ནམ་མཁའ་ལྟ་བུ་ཡང་ཟ་བ་པོར་རིགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ་ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །

Nor is it a connection through cause and effect, because happiness and so forth are seen to arise by degrees. It is illogical for an effect whose causes are not incomplete to sometimes arise or not arise, because there is no difference. For the self, which cannot be differentiated by others or possesses independent power, there is no dependence on a cooperative cause, by which it would arise by degrees in dependence on a cooperative cause. Therefore, if it is bound by being the cause that generates suffering, then at that time it would be bound at all times and would not become liberated, because it would not thoroughly abandon such a kind of nature. If it thoroughly abandons it, how would it become permanent? However, if it is liberated by being the cause that generates a state without suffering, then at that time it would exactly become liberated; if it is never bound, then at that time how could one thoroughly impute a bondage and liberation that have a basis? Likewise, if it is an agent by performing the characteristic of intention and so forth or by being capable of generating them, then at that time it would become an agent at all times, so how would it become an enjoyer? But if it is an enjoyer by being the cause that generates happiness and so forth, then at that time it would exactly become an enjoyer, so how would it become an agent? That which is thoroughly conceptualized by the Sāṃkhyas, unchanging like space due to happiness and so forth, is also not endowed with the logic to be an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd.

If it changes, permanence itself degenerates. Merely by being a cause it does not become an agent and an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd. Likewise, one should apply that a rememberer and so forth are also unsuitable to possess that as a basis. Therefore, it is only in the position that advocates selflessness that the presentation of liberation, bondage, and so forth is endowed with logic, because that presentation is thoroughly differentiated merely by the difference of cause and effect. That entity of cause and effect also is possible only for the impermanent, but not for the permanent, because they lack the power to generate any effect by degrees, just as explained before. Nor simultaneously, because the nature of the power to generate such a kind of effect follows again, and thus it is illogical to be separated from generating the effect just like before. If it does not follow, the prior nature would degenerate. Other than successive and simultaneous, there is no other aspect by which it would perform a function, because those two have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. For that very reason, whatever is non-momentary, whatever entities such as space are thoroughly conceptualized by others, all of them are objects of the convention of non-existence because they lack the capacity to perform a function—so the great Buddhist scholars state.

heading: ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྦྱོར་བའི་དབང་དུ་མཛད་པ།
translation: By way of application to the perfections, he spoke the words 'Moreover' and so forth. That too should be seen as the nature of two phrases having the nature of a general rule and an exception: this is the meaning of saying that a bodhisattva should indeed give a gift, but not by abiding in entities. By this term 'gift,' through the medium of the three types of giving, all six perfections are taught, not just giving alone. Herein, the giving of material things teaches the perfection of giving. The giving of fearlessness teaches the perfections of moral discipline and patience. The giving of Dharma teaches the perfections of effort, concentration, and wisdom: if there is no effort, one becomes thoroughly weary of retaining and teaching the Dharma, and thus will not teach the Dharma; if there is no concentration, because one desires what is more than faith, one will become an afflicted teacher; if there is no wisdom, one will teach it erroneously. Therefore, if all three are absent, the giving of Dharma will not be accomplished. Others explain that effort goes everywhere. By saying 'should give a gift,' it teaches how to abide in the six perfections through aspiration and prayer.

Nor is it a connection through cause and effect, because happiness and so forth are seen to arise by degrees. It is illogical for an effect whose causes are not incomplete to sometimes arise or not arise, because there is no difference. For the self, which cannot be differentiated by others or possesses independent power, there is no dependence on a cooperative cause, by which it would arise by degrees in dependence on a cooperative cause. Therefore, if it is bound by being the cause that generates suffering, then at that time it would be bound at all times and would not become liberated, because it would not thoroughly abandon such a kind of nature. If it thoroughly abandons it, how would it become permanent? However, if it is liberated by being the cause that generates a state without suffering, then at that time it would exactly become liberated; if it is never bound, then at that time how could one thoroughly impute a bondage and liberation that have a basis? Likewise, if it is an agent by performing the characteristic of intention and so forth or by being capable of generating them, then at that time it would become an agent at all times, so how would it become an enjoyer? But if it is an enjoyer by being the cause that generates happiness and so forth, then at that time it would exactly become an enjoyer, so how would it become an agent? That which is thoroughly conceptualized by the Sāṃkhyas, unchanging like space due to happiness and so forth, is also not endowed with the logic to be an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd.

If it changes, permanence itself degenerates. Merely by being a cause it does not become an agent and an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd. Likewise, one should apply that a rememberer and so forth are also unsuitable to possess that as a basis. Therefore, it is only in the position that advocates selflessness that the presentation of liberation, bondage, and so forth is endowed with logic, because that presentation is thoroughly differentiated merely by the difference of cause and effect. That entity of cause and effect also is possible only for the impermanent, but not for the permanent, because they lack the power to generate any effect by degrees, just as explained before. Nor simultaneously, because the nature of the power to generate such a kind of effect follows again, and thus it is illogical to be separated from generating the effect just like before. If it does not follow, the prior nature would degenerate. Other than successive and simultaneous, there is no other aspect by which it would perform a function, because those two have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. For that very reason, whatever is non-momentary, whatever entities such as space are thoroughly conceptualized by others, all of them are objects of the convention of non-existence because they lack the capacity to perform a function—so the great Buddhist scholars state.

[3-33] translation already produced for this document:
Imputing the convention of non-existence to a rabbit's horn and so forth is also due to the cause of merely lacking the capacity to perform a function. By implication, the object to which the convention of existence is imputed is exactly what is capable of performing a function, because existence and non-existence have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. If one imputes the name 'entity' even to that which is empty of all capacities of such a kind and is no different from a rabbit's horn and so forth, there is no dispute about names. However, those endowed with understanding of the meaningless assertion state that it is illogical to impute the convention of entity to such a kind of unobservable nature, which is no different from the son of a barren woman and so forth. Therefore, the reason is not unestablished. Because it would absurdly follow that space and so forth are also agents, it is also not inconclusive. Because it exists in what is harmonious with the position, it is also not contradictory. Because there is also no other characteristic of the self, therefore it is similar to the son of a barren woman. As for persons, too, if they perish, it would absurdly follow that they are included exactly within the aggregates, because the aggregates include all conditioned things. But if they do not perish, then at that time, by being dissimilar to the dharmas belonging to the aggregates, they would become exactly another entity from them, and the faults of that have already been stated. Therefore, there is no entity whatsoever that is called inexpressible. Therefore, the lion's roar of the Bhagavan, 'all dharmas are selfless,' terrifies all the herds of tīrthika elephants and is invincible, so there is no need for much.

heading: ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སྦྱོར་བའི་དབང་དུ་མཛད་པ།
translation: By "not abiding in entities" and so forth, it is taught how this is to be accomplished by entering into yogic equipoise. By "a bodhisattva should thus give a gift" and so forth, it is taught how, having annihilated distraction, the mind should be thoroughly apprehended. Herein, by "not abiding in entities," the reality of the application to the perfections is taught. Adhering as reality to entities such as the gift to be given, the giver, and the receiver is "abiding"; therefore, if a bodhisattva applies to the perfections after adhering to entities, it will become a wrong application, because they erroneously adhere while ultimately there is no entity whatsoever to which adherence would occur. This is because there is no valid cognition that establishes that, and because there is that which subverts it. Thus, that others ultimately assert the entity of an object as different from consciousness is, for a start, not established by direct perception, because it is illogical for an object that is other to be apprehended by consciousness. If the apprehension of an object by consciousness were to become one of three positions—with an aspect, without an aspect, or with another's aspect—for a start, it is not "with an aspect," because when seeing a multicolored mat and so forth, since they are not different from the single consciousness, it would absurdly follow that the aspects too have the nature of being single; or, since the consciousness too is not different from the aspects, it would absurdly follow that it has the nature of being multiple, just like the nature of the aspects.

འགྱུར་ན་ནི་རྟག་པ་ཉིད་ཉམས་སོ། །རྒྱུ་ཙམ་གྱིས་ནི་བྱེད་པ་པོ་དང་ཟ་བ་པོར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། ཧ་ཅང་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་དྲན་པ་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཡང་དེའི་གཞི་ཅན་དུ་མི་རུང་ཞེས་སྦྱར་བར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བདག་མེད་པར་སྨྲ་བའི་ཕྱོགས་ཁོ་ན་ལ་ཐར་པ་དང་བཅིངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་རྣམ་པར་གཞག་པ་རིགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་ཏེ། རྣམ་པར་གཞག་པ་དེ་རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་བྱེ་བྲག་ཙམ་གྱིས་རབ་ཏུ་ཕྱེ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །རྒྱུ་དང་འབྲས་བུའི་དངོས་པོ་དེ་ཡང་མི་རྟག་པ་ཁོ་ན་ལ་སྲིད་ཀྱི་རྟག་པ་རྣམས་ལ་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་དག་ལ་འབྲས་བུ་གང་ལ་ཡང་རིམ་གྱིས་བསྐྱེད་པའི་མཐུ་མེད་དེ། སྔར་ཇི་སྐད་བཤད་པ་བཞིན་ནོ། །ཅིག་ཅར་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། ཡང་རྣམ་པ་དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་འབྲས་བུ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་མཐུའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་སྟེ། སྔ་མ་བཞིན་དུ་འབྲས་བུ་བསྐྱེད་པ་དང་བྲལ་བར་མི་རིགས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །རྗེས་སུ་མི་འབྲང་ན་ནི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་སྔ་མ་ཉམས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །རིམ་དང་ཅིག་ཅར་དག་ལས་མ་གཏོགས་པ་གང་གིས་དོན་བྱེད་པར་འགྱུར་བའི་རྣམ་པ་གཞན་ནི་མེད་དེ། དེ་གཉིས་ནི་ཕན་ཚུན་སྤངས་ཏེ་གནས་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་སྐད་ཅིག་པ་མ་ཡིན་པ་གང་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་དངོས་པོ་གཞན་གྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟགས་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ནི་དོན་བྱེད་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་མེད་པར་ཐ་སྙད་གདགས་པའི་ཡུལ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་མཁས་པ་ཆེན་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་པ་དག་སྨྲའོ། །

If it changes, permanence itself degenerates. Merely by being a cause it does not become an agent and an enjoyer, because it would be extremely absurd. Likewise, one should apply that a rememberer and so forth are also unsuitable to possess that as a basis. Therefore, it is only in the position that advocates selflessness that the presentation of liberation, bondage, and so forth is endowed with logic, because that presentation is thoroughly differentiated merely by the difference of cause and effect. That entity of cause and effect also is possible only for the impermanent, but not for the permanent, because they lack the power to generate any effect by degrees, just as explained before. Nor simultaneously, because the nature of the power to generate such a kind of effect follows again, and thus it is illogical to be separated from generating the effect just like before. If it does not follow, the prior nature would degenerate. Other than successive and simultaneous, there is no other aspect by which it would perform a function, because those two have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. For that very reason, whatever is non-momentary, whatever entities such as space are thoroughly conceptualized by others, all of them are objects of the convention of non-existence because they lack the capacity to perform a function—so the great Buddhist scholars state.

རི་བོང་གི་རྭ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་མེད་པར་ཐ་སྙད་འདོགས་པ་ཡང་དོན་བྱེད་པའི་ནུས་པ་མེད་པ་ཙམ་གྱི་རྒྱུའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཤུགས་ཀྱིས་ན་ཡོད་པར་ཐ་སྙད་གདགས་པ་དོན་བྱེད་ནུས་པའི་ཡུལ་ཉིད་དེ། ཡོད་པ་དང་མེད་པ་ནི་ཕན་ཚུན་སྤངས་ཏེ་གནས་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །རྣམ་པ་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་ནུས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་པ་རི་བོང་གི་རྭ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པ་ལ་ཡང་དངོས་པོ་ཞེས་མིང་དུ་འདོགས་ན་ནི་མིང་ལ་ནི་བརྩད་པ་མེད་དོ། །འོན་ཀྱང་དོན་མེད་པའི་འདོད་པ་རྟོགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དག་ནི་རྣམ་པ་དེ་ལྟ་བུ་མི་དམིགས་པའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་མོ་གཤམ་གྱི་བུ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པ་ལ་དངོས་པོར་ཐ་སྙད་འདོགས་པ་རིགས་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་སྨྲའོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་གཏན་ཚིགས་མ་གྲུབ་པ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་ཡང་བྱེད་པ་པོར་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་བས་མ་ངེས་པ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །ཕྱོགས་དང་མཐུན་པ་ལ་ཡོད་པས་འགལ་བ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །བདག་གི་མཚན་ཉིད་གཞན་ཡང་མེད་པས་དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་མོ་གཤམ་གྱི་བུ་དང་འདྲའོ། །གང་ཟག་དག་ཀྱང་གལ་ཏེ་འཇིག་ན་ནི་ཕུང་པོ་རྣམས་ཁོ་ནའི་ནང་དུ་འདུས་པར་ཐལ་བར་འགྱུར་སྟེ། ཕུང་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་འདུས་བྱས་མཐའ་དག་བསྡུས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །འོན་ཏེ་མི་འཇིག་ན་དེའི་ཚེ་ཕུང་པོར་གཏོགས་པའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་དང་མི་འདྲ་བས་དེ་ལས་དོན་གཞན་པ་ཁོ་ནར་འགྱུར་ཏེ། དེའི་ཉེས་པ་ནི་བརྗོད་ཟིན་ཏོ། །དེ་ལྟ་བས་ན་བརྗོད་དུ་མི་རུང་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་དངོས་པོ་ཅུང་ཟད་ཀྱང་མེད་དེ། དེས་ན་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་བདག་མེད་དོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱི་སེང་གེའི་སྒྲ་ནི་མུ་སྟེགས་བྱེད་གླང་པོ་ཆེའི་ཁྱུ་མཐའ་དག་སྐྲག་པར་མཛད་ཅིང་བརྫི་བ་མེད་པ་ཡིན་པས་མང་དུ་མི་དགོས་སོ། །

Imputing the convention of non-existence to a rabbit's horn and so forth is also due to the cause of merely lacking the capacity to perform a function. By implication, the object to which the convention of existence is imputed is exactly what is capable of performing a function, because existence and non-existence have the characteristic of abiding by mutually excluding each other. If one imputes the name 'entity' even to that which is empty of all capacities of such a kind and is no different from a rabbit's horn and so forth, there is no dispute about names. However, those endowed with understanding of the meaningless assertion state that it is illogical to impute the convention of entity to such a kind of unobservable nature, which is no different from the son of a barren woman and so forth. Therefore, the reason is not unestablished. Because it would absurdly follow that space and so forth are also agents, it is also not inconclusive. Because it exists in what is harmonious with the position, it is also not contradictory. Because there is also no other characteristic of the self, therefore it is similar to the son of a barren woman. As for persons, too, if they perish, it would absurdly follow that they are included exactly within the aggregates, because the aggregates include all conditioned things. But if they do not perish, then at that time, by being dissimilar to the dharmas belonging to the aggregates, they would become exactly another entity from them, and the faults of that have already been stated. Therefore, there is no entity whatsoever that is called inexpressible. Therefore, the lion's roar of the Bhagavan, 'all dharmas are selfless,' terrifies all the herds of tīrthika elephants and is invincible, so there is no need for much.
